data.description:
## Observation
`make verify` fails with **17 test failures** on an Apple Silicon (arm64) macOS host, on a **clean tree** at `6a0e3c9afcd` with zero local changes:

- `tests/unit/reconciler/test_wiki_render.py` — 13 failures (incl. `test_pypandoc_and_pandoc_versions_are_pinned`, the 5 `test_real_jira_writer_output_shapes` cases, `test_dc_*`)
- `tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py` — 3 failures
- `tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py::test_the_rendered_form_really_does_differ`

Root cause, confirmed directly:

```
OSError: [Errno 86] Bad CPU type in executable:
  .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pypandoc/files/pandoc
```

The installed distribution is `pypandoc_binary-1.17`, and its wheel tag is **correct** for the host:

```
Tag: py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64
```

but the pandoc executable **inside** that arm64 wheel is x86_64:

```
pypandoc/files/pandoc: Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64
```

So this is not a dependency-resolution mistake in rebar's lock — uv selected the right wheel for the platform. It is an **upstream packaging defect in `pypandoc_binary` 1.17**: the macOS arm64 wheel ships an x86_64 pandoc binary.

Rosetta is not functional on the affected host (`/usr/bin/arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true` → `Bad CPU type in executable`), so the bundled binary cannot execute at all. On a host **with** Rosetta the same wheel would run translated and the tests would pass, which is why this is invisible to some machines and to Linux CI.

`_pandoc_path()` (`src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py`) returns `None` when `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()` raises `OSError`, and `test_pypandoc_and_pandoc_versions_are_pinned` is deliberately written so "a drifted or absent pandoc must FAIL here, never silently skip" — so the failure mode is correct and intended; only the binary is wrong.

## Impact
`make verify` is the stated pre-push contract and the locally checkable half of `Verified`. On an arm64 Mac without Rosetta it cannot go green on an unmodified tree, so every agent and contributor on that hardware either cannot satisfy the contract or learns to ignore 17 red tests — which erodes the suite as a regression oracle. CI (`ubuntu-latest`) is unaffected, so nothing catches it.

## Verified workaround (applied locally, not committed)
Replacing the wheel's binary with the official native build of the **same pinned version** turns all 17 green:

```sh
curl -sL -o p.zip https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/download/3.9/pandoc-3.9-arm64-macOS.zip
unzip -q p.zip && cp <extracted>/bin/pandoc \
  .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pypandoc/files/pandoc
```

`pandoc --version` then reports `pandoc 3.9`, satisfying the pin, and
`pytest tests/unit/reconciler/test_wiki_render.py tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py -q` reports **74 passed**.

The workaround is per-venv, so it is lost on every `make worktree`.

## Proposed fix (needs a decision before implementation)
Options, in rough order of preference:

1. **Verify the bundled binary's architecture at env-bootstrap time** — have `make install` / `make venv` check `file`/`mach-o` arch of `pypandoc/files/pandoc` against `uname -m` and, on mismatch, fetch the pinned native pandoc into the venv. Fixes every worktree automatically; adds a bootstrap step.
2. **Pin plain `pypandoc` (no bundled binary) plus a documented host pandoc 3.9**, letting `_pandoc_path()` resolve from `PATH`. Removes the broken-wheel dependency entirely; shifts a setup burden onto contributors and CI.
3. **Document it in `docs/local-dev-env.md` only** — cheapest, but leaves `make verify` red by default on affected hardware, which is the condition that caused this ticket.

Option 1 is portable (no CI-provider coupling) and keeps the existing pin; it is the recommended direction but is NOT yet decided.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On an arm64 macOS host without Rosetta, a freshly provisioned worktree (`make worktree name=<x>`) resolves a pandoc binary whose architecture matches `uname -m`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/test_wiki_render.py tests/unit/reconciler/test_rich_text_cutover.py tests/unit/reconciler/diffing/test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py -q` reports 74 passed on that host with no manual intervention.
- [ ] `test_pypandoc_and_pandoc_versions_are_pinned` still asserts `pypandoc.__version__ == "1.17"` and `pandoc 3.9`, and still FAILS (never skips) when pandoc is absent or drifted.
- [ ] The fix introduces no CI-provider-specific trigger: it runs from the documented local bootstrap, not only from a GitHub Actions step.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0 on an unmodified tree on arm64 macOS.
data.title: make verify fails with 17 reconciler failures on arm64 macOS: pypandoc_binary 1.17's arm64 wheel ships an x86_64 pandoc
